classification.difficultyReason: Students interpret the diagram's 135-degree inclination as gradient −1, solve the derivative condition, and use the resulting point to form the tangent equation.

inlines.text: and a tangent to the curve is shown below.
Find the equation of the tangent.

spec.sourceRegion: Upper-right question 41 graph, between the introductory sentence and response instruction
spec.description: Unticked Cartesian axes labelled x and y, a blue exponential curve with downward-directed endpoint arrows, and a black descending tangent. Its inclination from the positive x-direction to the upper-left tangent ray is labelled 135 degrees.
spec.mathematics: Plot y=6x-2e^x mathematically. The tangent has slope tan(135 degrees)=-1 and touches the curve at x=ln(7/2). Its equation is used only to construct the supplied line and is not printed.
spec.answerVisibility: The student figure shows the supplied curve, tangent and angle only; no tangent equation or point coordinates are displayed.

inlines.text: to locate the point of tangency.

answer.worked:
The tangent's gradient is $m=\tan135^\circ=-1$.

$$y'=6-2e^x$$

At the point of tangency,

$$\begin{align*}6-2e^x&=-1\\2e^x&=7\\e^x&=\frac72\\x&=\ln\left(\frac72\right).\end{align*}$$

Substituting into the curve gives

$$y=6\ln\left(\frac72\right)-7.$$

The tangent equation is

$$\begin{align*}y-\left(6\ln\left(\frac72\right)-7\right)&=-\left(x-\ln\left(\frac72\right)\right)\\y&=-x+7\ln\left(\frac72\right)-7.\end{align*}$$
